cim: Australia turns to MIT to solve its productivity problem: AI adoption
cim_eredeti: Australia turns to MIT to solve its productivity problem: AI adoption
szoveg_eredeti:
Researchers will use data from Australia's biggest bank to determine if artificial intelligence is making firms more productive

CANBERRA — The Australian Bureau of Statistics is teaming up with the Commonwealth Bank to help researchers from the Massachusetts Institute Technology study anonymized business banking data, to better measure artificial intelligence adoption in Australia’s private sector.

The Productivity Commission — the Australian government’s economic think tank — has warned that AI adoption in Australia is lagging other comparable countries. The Reserve Bank of Australia has found a massive increase in the proportion of businesses experimenting with the technology, but it believes ongoing adoption is limited.

On Oct. 28 the ABS notified that it plans to collect aggregated monthly expenditure activity data of Australian businesses held by the Commonwealth Bank from January 2019 onwards, for public interest research and statistical analysis purposes.

That will include the identity of the business, transaction month and year and the amounts spent on categories including AI and information technology. It will be made available to researchers from 2027.
